mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when inflation expectations rise sharply (CPIAUCSL > 4% YoY).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or GDP growth rebounds above 2% in the following quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid deceleration in payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) below 50k new jobs per month for three consecutive months signals labor market softening, which pressures corporate margins and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change < 50k for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the labor market shows simultaneous wage acceleration (HOUST > 2% YoY).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness, which reduces corporate earnings and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the contraction is accompanied by a simultaneous surge in commodity prices (HOUST > 10% YoY).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (inflation) above their respective 12-month averages signals a stagflationary tightening, which depresses equity valuations due to higher real discount rates and eroded purchasing power, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving average in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of triggered months, or CPIAUCSL falls below 2% YoY after the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) for two consecutive months signals a broad-based deterioration in demand, which lowers earnings expectations and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both fall month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the decline in HOUST reverses within the next month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6.5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market constraint, which reduces corporate profit margins and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or UNRATE falls below 6% within the next quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (implied by RSAFS rising above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months) signals elevated precautionary savings and weaker consumption momentum, which reduces corporate revenue growth and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month moving average for five consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 65% of triggered episodes, or RSAFS reverts to below its moving average within the next two months.
